classification.difficultyReason: Recognise equal ordinates at intersections and double their signed value to obtain points on the sum graph.

inlines.text: Explain how they are quickly obtained.

spec.description: Black axes with positive-direction arrowheads and x and y labels; two unlabelled smooth component curves and three isolated purple points. One point lies above the shared positive crest; two lie below later intersections. No grid, ticks, numerical scale or origin label.
spec.mathematics: Each supplied point keeps the x-coordinate of an intersection and doubles its common signed ordinate. The positive point lies twice as far above the x-axis; the two negative points lie twice as far below it. Drawing coordinates normalise the unscaled source sketch and do not specify equations or numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Both component curves and all three supplied purple points remain visible in the question edition.

answer.short: Where the graphs intersect, double their common ordinate and keep the same $x$-coordinate.
answer.worked: At each intersection, both graphs have the same ordinate. Add that ordinate to itself and keep the same $x$-coordinate; a negative ordinate doubles downwards.
